title: denial_reason_result.json -- insurer's stated position, grounds, and policy matches v0.5
description: Produced by denial-response. Each materially distinct insurer decision is a separate reason. decision_type records denial versus reduction; payment_status records the observed payment outcome independently. Every stated or inferred ground and every policy match carries source locations. v0.5 makes a SPLIT outcome expressible: decision_type/payment_status were always scoped to one claim coverage, but nothing recorded WHICH one, so a response denying one coverage while paying another could record only the denial -- and payment_status: unpaid then read as 'nothing was paid'. decided_coverage names the coverage a reason decides; accepted_coverages records what the same response accepted (an acceptance is neither a denial nor a reduction, so it cannot be a denial_reason). Both additive -- pre-2026-08-04 contracts validate unchanged, and a contract with no acceptances hashes identically to before. The optional upstream_policy_snapshot binds any policy-referencing result to the exact policy-layer digest set it consumed; the DAO requires and verifies it whenever a clause reference exists. Judgment-type output; include the safety fields from common_component_output.schema.json.

denial_reasons.description: Extracted reasons. Empty array means no denial/reduction found.

accepted_coverages.description: owner: denial-response. Coverages the insurer ACCEPTED, recorded only when the same response also denies or reduces something else. An acceptance is neither a denial nor a reduction, so it has no decision_type and cannot be filed as a denial_reason -- but leaving it out is what makes a partial outcome read as a total one. CASE_907: the insurer denied 배상책임 and paid 2,000,000원 구내치료비, and the contract could record only the denial. Absent/empty means the response contained no acceptance, the ordinary case for a pure denial notice. Not a payout ledger: record only what the insurer's own response states, with the quote that states it.

upstream_policy_snapshot.description: The policy-layer snapshot this artifact was derived from (Part 11I). Required whenever the artifact carries at least one policy reference: a downstream result is an assertion about what the policy layer said when it was written, so it records which bytes it read. The DAO recomputes this at write time and refuses a mismatch; `dao.py policy-snapshot` prints the current value. Per-document digests cover the normalized contract, boundary inventory, reference tables, processed source text, manifest entry (page_map included) and governing parent coverage -- the same set the document's audit binds to.

accepted_coverage.description: One coverage the insurer accepted in a response that denies or reduces something else. Deliberately thin: this exists to stop a partial outcome reading as a total one, not to become a second decision record. It carries no taxonomy_code (the taxonomy classifies denial/reduction grounds, and an acceptance has none) and no grounds/rebuttal surface, because nothing here is disputed.

coverage_name.description: The coverage in the insurer's own wording, e.g. '구내치료비'. Matches the vocabulary decided_coverage uses on a denial reason so the two sides of a split outcome can be read together.

payment_status.description: The observed outcome for THIS coverage. 'paid' or 'partially_paid' is the normal case here; 'unknown' is legitimate when the insurer states acceptance but no payment confirmation appears in the response.

accepted_amount.description: The amount the insurer states it pays for this coverage, or null when the response accepts without naming a figure. Never inferred, computed, or carried over from a claim document -- if the insurer did not state it, it is null.

insurer_stated_basis.description: The insurer's own stated reason for accepting, when it gives one (e.g. that the clause pays irrespective of legal liability). null when it simply pays without explanation.

policy_matches.description: The clause the acceptance rests on, when identifiable. Same shape and same verification as a denial reason's matches -- an acceptance grounded in a clause that does not exist is no better than a denial grounded that way. Empty is fine; an unsupported link must not be invented.

evidence_references.description: Where in the insurer's response the acceptance is stated. Required: an acceptance nobody can locate in the source is exactly the unverifiable claim P1 forbids.

basis_source.description: Never merge an insurer-stated ground with an agent-inferred ground. agent_inferred always requires expert review.

evidence_references.description: Exact source location supporting this basis text. A basis without a source location is invalid, not merely low-confidence.

grounds.description: Three non-overlapping ground categories. Empty arrays mean the insurer response did not state that kind of ground; never fill an absent ground by guesswork.

amounts.description: Explicit payment amounts. Use null when the insurer response does not state a value; do not infer one.

match_source.description: insurer_cited means the insurer response identifies the clause; agent_inferred means the agent found a potentially relevant clause and must route it for review.

insurer_citation_evidence_references.description: Location in the insurer response where the clause was cited. Empty only for agent_inferred matches.

policy_clause_evidence_references.description: Location of the matched clause in the processed policy document. Required for every match so denial-validation can verify the link before relying on it.

decided_coverage.description: owner: denial-response. WHICH claim coverage or claim item this decision is about, in the insurer's own wording (e.g. '배상책임', '구내치료비'). decision_type and payment_status have always been scoped to 'one claim coverage or claim item', never to the case -- but nothing recorded which one, so a reader had to assume the reason covered the whole claim. That assumption misreads the ordinary case where an insurer denies one coverage and pays another: CASE_907's insurer denied 배상책임 while paying 2,000,000원 구내치료비 under a clause that pays '보통약관 제3조의 규정에도 불구하고', i.e. independently of legal liability. Recording only the denial left payment_status: unpaid to be read as 'nothing was paid'. Required for every new reason; absent on pre-2026-08-04 contracts, which were written when a case was implicitly assumed to be single-coverage.

candidate_codes.description: Ranked classification candidates, best first. Required and non-empty: this is the Top-1/Top-3 evaluation input, and an omitted list silently removes a reason from that measurement rather than scoring it. The first entry must equal taxonomy_code (the headline code IS the top candidate -- a list whose winner disagrees with the assigned code describes a classification nobody made), codes must be distinct, and confidence must be non-increasing. Descending order and the top-1 match are checked by the DAO's cross-contract validator, which can compare siblings; JSON Schema can only pin shape.

allOf.description: Reduction-only codes must not be classified as denial.
Denial-only codes must not be classified as reduction.
R12 and R14 remain unclassified pending adjuster confirmation and always require review whichever decision type the source supports.
